records.title: Identity, Cooperation and Framing Effects within Groups of Real and Simulated Humans
records.reason: The original contribution is an empirical social-behavior simulation study of U.S. partisan Dictator/Trust games and framing/date/participant effects. Narrative deep binding and demographic matching reuse the cited anthology method; temporal prompt grounding and an LLM consistency critic are study controls, not a new independently specified general agent algorithm. No new released public benchmark/framework was verified; AppendixF promises future code/prompts/backstories. Preserve this scientific study as a sourceful exclusion, not a high-cost reproduction falsely advertised as accepted. This does not deny its empirical contribution.
records.cost_context_only: Authors use eight RTX A6000/A5000 with 24B/70B base models and Gemini critic; no run attempted. Cost is not the selection reason.
